maria: quick heads-up — canary on mixed-gpu cluster regressed ~18% p99 for seqlen≈96 workloads after yesterday's kernel-autopick change. looks like the picker is choosing the fp8-small-matmul path on some SM89 boxes and that path thrashes KV cache.
noah: can you paste the probe output and a perf snippet? wondering if it's mis-detecting fp8 support or just choosing wrong heuristic for mid-lengths.
maria: pasted perf and probe below — short summary first: SM=89, driver reports fp8 capability but microbench shows fp8 kernel slower for seq≈96 due to increased L2 / kvcache eviction. attaching logs inline.

maria: ```
# device_probe --json /dev/nvidia0
{
  "sm": 89,
  "tensor_cores": true,
  "bf16_supported": true,
  "fp8_supported_reported": true,
  "driver_version": "540.32",
  "pci_bus": "0000:3b:00.0"
}
```

maria: ```
# simple microbench (seqlen=96, bs=8)
kernel chosen: fp8_small_gemm_fast
tokens/sec: 42k
kvcache miss rate: 0.24
L2 evictions/sec: 1.9k

fallback (bf16_fastpath):
tokens/sec: 51k
kvcache miss rate: 0.03
L2 evictions/sec: 0.4k
```

raj: hmm driver reports fp8 but perf says otherwise — could be that fp8 kernels allocate larger workspace or use a blocking tiling that clashes with our kvcache layout on SM89. also some BIOS-firmware combos expose fp8 bits even though tc kernels slower.
lucy: can we add a quick runtime microprobe that benchmarks a tiny 1-2-step matmul and a KV access pattern during node startup? then cache that result per-machine-id for 1h.
noah: +1. suggest two parts: (1) capability_probe stays as-is for feature bits; (2) add lightweight perf_probe for seqlen buckets {1-32,33-128,129+} that returns preferred kernel tag and a confidence score. picker merges: if perf_probe.confidence>0.6 prefer; else fall back to heuristic.
maria: implementation note — keep perf_probe <=15ms per model to avoid startup hit. sample command:

maria: ```
# perf_probe --seqlen 96 --bs 4 --workload kv-lite
> PREF=fp8_small_gemm_fast
> latency=3.8ms
> mem_scratch=12MB
> kv_evictions=significant
```

raj: also add a small safety: if kv_evictions > threshold then penalize kernel by -0.2 confidence so mixed farms don't pick fp8 for seqlen in [48,128].
noah: I'll sketch the picker merge logic and a change-set: 
- add perf_probe module (golang) calling a tiny cuda kernel
- persist per-device results under /var/lib/redwood/device-probe
- expose probe override in runtime config: kernel_picker.force_override={}

lucy: can we also log seqlen histogram per model route (sample 1% requests) to inform heuristic thresholds? that would help automatic tuning in Optimize.
maria: agreed — we'll sample and aggregate to console dashboards. also plan a canary rollout: enable perf_probe fallback for 10% of traffic on dedicated canary pool.
deploy-bot: canary deployment started: canary/kvprobe-v1 -> 3169001250
noah: action items: (1) noah implement perf_probe draft (ETA tomorrow morning) (2) raj add kv_eviction metric in low-overhead sampler (ETA EOD) (3) maria run canary and collect 1h traces (ETA +6h) (4) lucy add seqlen histogram pipeline (ETA next sprint)
maria: thanks — will post results here. if perf_probe shows fp8 is actually ok for shorter seqlens we can tighten threshold. :thumbsup:
